fact: The Ministry of Transport and Communications' National Broadband Strategy says Botswana has a fibre optic backbone network in the form of a ring owned by BoFiNet, with private operators such as Mascom also having deployed national backbone infrastructure; it describes the backbone as connecting all urban centres and major villages (document gives June 2018 publication date, no earlier date).
BoFiNet reported at its 13 August 2026 AGM 99.7% service availability across its national fibre backbone (News&All Botswana report, no regions or km given).
The article describes BoFiNet's national mandate as the country's wholesale open-access fibre and broadband infrastructure provider; buyers are not named.

Communications minister David Tshere said approximately 16,000 km of fibre optic cable is already laid across Botswana, linking the country internally and to South Africa, Namibia, Zimbabwe and Zambia; the document gives no towns or regions and does not say 'lit' or name the owner (published date used as as_of).
